questions.prompt: A loop() ends with delay(500) and also polls a push button. Short taps on the button are often ignored. What is the best fix?
options: Lower the Serial baud rate so printing takes less time.
Raise the delay so the loop runs less often.
Drop delay() and act only when now - last >= period.
Replace the button with a faster switch part.
questions.explanation: The button is read only once per delay period, so a tap shorter than the delay is often missed. Scheduling with millis() lets the loop pass hundreds of times per second.

questions.prompt: An Uno runs analogWrite(pin, 64). What duty cycle is that, in percent? Precision 0.1.
An Uno ADC (5 V reference, 10 bit) reads 307. What is the input voltage in volts? Precision 0.005.
Which test is safe across the 32-bit rollover of millis()?
options: now - last >= period, all unsigned long
questions.explanation: Unsigned subtraction is modulo 2^32, so now - last stays correct after now wraps past zero.

questions.prompt: ESP32 LEDC runs from an 80 MHz clock. What is the maximum duty resolution in bits at 10 kHz?
A sensor outputs 5 V logic. How should it connect to an ESP32 input?
options: Directly: the internal pull-up limits the current.
Through an ADC2 pin, which protects the input.
Through a divider or level shifter to 3.3 V.
questions.explanation: ESP32 pins are 3.3 V and not 5 V tolerant, so a divider or level shifter is needed.

questions.prompt: A sketch blinks an LED with delay(500) and checks a button once per loop pass. Describe how to restructure it so both react promptly, and name one hazard to avoid.
rubric: Removes delay() and calls both jobs on every pass of loop().
Keeps a last-time variable per job and tests now - last >= period, then advances last by the period.
Names a hazard: rollover with signed or summed comparisons, a hidden delay or long print, or int overflow.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
